title: Function Definition and Notation
notes: **Formal definition:** Let X and Y be two non-empty sets. Then a function f from X to Y is a rule which assigns a **unique** element of Y to each element of X.
**Notation:** We write f: X → Y to denote 'f is a function from X to Y'. This is read as 'f maps X to Y'.
**Image notation:** The unique element of Y which f assigns corresponding to an element x in X is denoted by f(x). We also write y = f(x) to show the relationship.
**Domain:** The set X from which elements are taken is called the domain of the function f. It contains all possible input values.
**Codomain:** The set Y to which elements are mapped is called the codomain of f. It contains all possible output values (though not all may be achieved).
**Image (Range subset):** The element f(x) of Y, corresponding to x in X, is called the image of x under the function f.
**Key property:** Each input x in the domain must have exactly ONE output f(x) in the codomain. A relation is NOT a function if any input maps to multiple outputs.
**Visual representation:** Functions can be represented as arrows from domain elements to codomain elements, or as graphs showing the relationship between x and f(x).
confusion: A function requires UNIQUE assignment — one input cannot map to multiple outputs. Relations that do this are not functions.
Domain and codomain are different concepts: domain is the set of all inputs, codomain is the set of all possible outputs.
Notation f: X → Y does NOT mean f equals something — it means 'f is a function from set X to set Y'.
f(x) is the value of the function at x, not f multiplied by x. The parentheses indicate function application, not multiplication.
Multiple inputs can map to the same output (many-to-one), but one input cannot map to multiple outputs (one-to-many is not allowed).
practice: Given f: {1, 2, 3} → {a, b, c} defined by f(1) = a, f(2) = b, f(3) = a, identify the domain, codomain, and all images.
Which of these relations are functions? (a) {(1,a), (2,b), (1,c)} (b) {(1,a), (2,b), (3,c)} (c) {(1,a), (2,b), (2,c)}
Write the function notation for: 'The rule that assigns to each real number its square'.
If f: ℝ → ℝ is defined by f(x) = 2x + 1, find f(3), f(-1), and f(0). What is the domain and codomain?
Explain why the relation {(1,2), (2,3), (3,4)} is a function but {(1,2), (1,3), (2,4)} is not.
universalFacts: Functions are the fundamental building blocks of mathematics — all of calculus is built on the concept of functions.
The concept of a function was formalized in the 17th century by Leibniz and Euler, though the idea was used implicitly earlier.
Every equation y = f(x) defines a function, but not every relation defines a function (use the vertical line test on graphs).
Functions appear everywhere: physics (position as function of time), economics (cost as function of quantity), computer science (input-output mappings).
The notation f(x) was introduced by Euler in 1734 and has been standard ever since.
